clinician.final_diagnosis: well-differentiated low-grade neuroendocrine tumor of the liver confirmed by percutaneous biopsy with immunohistochemistry
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 51-year-old man presented with systemic symptoms including nausea, headache, vomiting, malaise, and significant weight loss, along with severe hypercalcemia >15 mg/dl, low PTH, low vitamin D, and acute kidney injury. Imaging via EUS showed a large heterogeneous pancreatic mass (51x37 mm) with arterial involvement and multiple large heterogeneous liver lesions. Percutaneous liver biopsy demonstrated a well-differentiated low-grade neuroendocrine tumor confirmed by immunohistochemistry (positive chromogranin and synaptophysin, negative CK20, CK7, LCA, and Ki-67 index <3%). The patient was treated with octreotide and everolimus; surgical options were discussed but declined.
